lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Traffic on the eights. One hundred and fourteen point eight. Every ten minutes, whether you're moving or not.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: This is Traffic on the eights. Rita Gridley, at the desk. Nothing is moving. Here's how.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Captain Buzz Ferraro, in the pod, over the junction. You're listening to Traffic on the eights.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Traffic on the eights. Wormholes, timelines and the bypass. Mostly the bypass.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: One one four point eight. Traffic on the eights. The jam's been here since the Big Bang, and so, it feels like, have I.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Traffic on the eights, through the night. The lanes are quiet. The bypass is not. The bypass is never quiet.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Traffic on the eights. Rita Gridley at the desk. Here's how it isn't moving.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: It's that time again. It's always that time again. Traffic.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Your traffic and travel, every ten minutes, on the eights. Eyes on the road you're on. It isn't going anywhere.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Traffic now. If you're listening in a vehicle, you've got time. Trust me.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Traffic on the eights. Same jam, fresh report.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Here's the traffic, brought to you by the traffic. It sponsors itself. Nobody else will go near it.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Let's go straight up to Buzz in the pod.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Morning, Rita. Or evening. Hard to say from up here.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: It's always hard to say, Buzz. Here's the traffic.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Late night traffic. Lighter in most lanes. Still solid on the bypass. Some things don't sleep.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: On the bypass, the gridlock that's been there since the Big Bang is still there. Delays of roughly fourteen billion years.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: The front car is still waiting for the lights to change. The lights haven't been invented yet. When they are, we'll let you know.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Long delays at the Great Wormhole Interchange. Junction nine is backed up to junction four, and junction four is backed up to last Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Allow plenty of time. And then allow a little extra time for the time.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Buzz, what are you seeing on the Outer Ring?

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Rita, I've got a jackknifed comet across both lanes, eastbound. Tail's everywhere.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Nobody's hurt. Everybody's slowing down to make a wish. That's what's causing the tailback. The wishing.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Slow traffic northbound past the Varn Nebula, where drivers are rubbernecking at a supernova on the hard shoulder.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: It's been going off for three days. Please keep your eyes on your lane. It'll still be exploding when you get home.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: In the timelines, a contraflow is in operation through the eleventh century.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: If you're heading for the twelfth, expect a diversion through a short Dark Age. Lights on, windows up, and please don't stop to help anybody build a cathedral. It takes ages.

clips.title: The Ring Road With One Side

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: On the ring road with only one side, the outside lane is also the inside lane.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: If you're overtaking, you are also being overtaken, by you. Drivers are asked to stop waving at themselves. It's distracting the other drivers, who are also you.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Lane two of the Hennick wormhole has been stuck in reverse since this morning. Drivers are arriving before they've set off.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: If you meet yourself at the other end, please don't discuss the journey. It spoils it for you.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: The Thursday flyover is closed for maintenance until Wednesday. Which Wednesday hasn't been confirmed.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Diversions are in place through Friday, which is busier than it looks. It always is.

clips.title: A Glacier in the Slow Lane

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: A glacier is moving slowly in the slow lane of the Ice Age Parkway.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: It's in the right lane. It's doing the right speed. It's just a very, very long vehicle. Patience, please. It'll be past you by the spring. Not this spring.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Lost property on the hard shoulder near exit forty. One moon. Small. Slightly dented. Answers to nothing.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: If it's yours, please collect it before it gets dark. It'll want to be up by then.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Rita, I've got a relay ship on the Outer Band approach. Drifting across the lanes, one at a time. No indicators. Running lights all on.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Is it lost, Buzz?

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Doesn't drive like it's lost, Rita. Drives like it knows the way, and it's in no hurry to get there.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: A broken-down star on the Long Straight is blocking the middle lane. Recovery is on the way.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Recovery has been on the way for some time. Recovery may, itself, have broken down. We're sending recovery for recovery.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: A pod of very slow space whales is crossing all lanes at the Drift.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: They have right of way. They have always had right of way. They were here first, and they'll tell you so, at length, in a low voice, for about an hour.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Roadworks on the Spiral Arm. Three lanes down to one, while a crew fills in a pothole that goes through to another dimension.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: They've filled it twice. It keeps filling them back. Expect delays, and a small amount of somebody else's gravel.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Buzz, how's it looking from up there?

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Rita, I've been circling this junction thirty one years, and I've just seen something I've never seen.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: A gap. Lane three. About a car's length.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Is it moving?

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: No, Rita. Somebody's already in it.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Drivers on the Big Bang approach should expect expansion. The road is getting longer while you drive on it.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: You are not going slower. Everything is simply further away than it was. It's not personal. It's the universe.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: We've got a commuter on the line from the bypass. Go ahead, caller.

lines.speaker: A Commuter
lines.text: Rita, I've been on the bypass since I was nine.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: How's it moving?

lines.speaker: A Commuter
lines.text: I moved up one, the summer I turned twenty. I still think about it.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Hold on to that. Thank you, caller.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Around the black hole at junction thirteen, traffic is approaching at normal speed, but appears, from outside, to slow to a complete stop.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: It isn't stopped. It only looks stopped. Unlike the bypass, which looks stopped because it is.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: On the parallel lanes, there's a version of you who left ten minutes earlier. They're making good progress.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Don't think about them. They're not thinking about you. They're nearly home.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Word from Waystation Nine dispatch. A wide load on the sideways road, and a strong suggestion from Big Rosalind that you don't take it.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: We agree. In thirty years on this desk, we've never once seen anybody come back from the sideways road on time. Or on the same day.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Rita, there's a phantom jam on the Old Lane. Nobody can see the front of it, because there's no front.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: It formed eleven years ago when somebody braked for a moth. The moth's long gone. The jam stayed. It likes it here.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: That's traffic. Next report in ten minutes, on the eights. The jam will still be there. It's very loyal.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: That's your traffic. Mirror, signal, wait. Mostly wait.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Traffic on the eights, back in ten. Stay in your lane. Everyone else is.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: That's the traffic for now. And for later. It's the same traffic. Back in ten.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: If you've moved since the last report, ring in. We'd love to hear how. Traffic on the eights.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: That's the traffic. Drive safely. Arrive eventually.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Buzz, anything to add?

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Negative, Rita.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Thank you, Buzz. Back in ten.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Back in ten minutes with more of the same. Rita Gridley, at the traffic desk.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: The weather for drivers. A brisk solar wind from the east, gusting to strong around the big yellow star at junction two.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: High-sided vessels, take care. Small ones, hold on to something. Anything with a sail, you'll be in the next system by tea time, and you won't have enjoyed it.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Scattered meteor showers over the Interchange this evening, heavier towards the bypass, where nobody is going anywhere anyway.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Wipers on. And if one lands on your bonnet, it's yours. That's the law out here. Finders keepers.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Rita, one just went past the pod. Didn't indicate. They never indicate.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Thick fog in the Varn Nebula overnight. Visibility down to about a planet's length.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Dipped headlights, please. Full beam just lights the fog up, and then the fog wants to talk to you about it.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: It's lonely, the fog. It means well. Just don't encourage it. Clearing by morning, or by the morning after.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: This morning, a slow-moving front of Tuesdays is pushing in from the timelines. Expect it to feel like Tuesday for most of the day, even where it isn't.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Clearing to Wednesday by the evening, for most of you. Some of you will be in Tuesday till the weekend. Sorry.

clips.title: Thirty One Years in the Pod

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Buzz, how long have you been up there now?

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Thirty one years, Rita. I land on my birthday. They bring me a cake and a fresh flask.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: And then?

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: And then I go back up. Somebody's got to watch it not move.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: People ask me what it's like to report on traffic that has never once moved.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: And I say, it's like any other job. You turn up. You look at it. You tell people how it is. And every ten minutes you hope, just a little, that this is the time.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Ten minutes is a long time in traffic. It's also no time at all. I've done a few million of them now.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: My advice? Bring a sandwich. Bring two. Bring somebody to share the second one with.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Rita, you ever hear the one about the old switchboard?

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Which one?

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Story goes there's an operator out past the edge of the dial, still putting calls through. She answers if you ring advice, then the news, then the traffic. In that order. Hold each line a moment.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: We're the traffic, Buzz.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: I know. I always wondered who was ringing.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: A message for the relay ship on the Outer Band tonight. Buzz can see your running lights from the pod.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: You're drifting across three lanes. We're not complaining. There's nobody in them. Just, wherever you're headed, indicate. It's polite.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Rita, my flask's empty.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: We'll send one up, Buzz.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: How long?

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Well. It'll have to go round by the bypass.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: I'll ration the biscuits.

lines.speaker: Advert
lines.text: Stuck on the bypass? Of course you are. Gridlock Grill comes to you.

lines.speaker: Advert
lines.text: Our waiters walk between the lanes with hot food, cold drinks and a smile that has been on duty for generations.

lines.speaker: Advert
lines.text: Gridlock Grill. Drive thru, at no miles an hour. Table for one? You've got the whole car.

lines.speaker: Advert
lines.text: Feeling the urge to change lanes? Don't. It won't help. It has never helped.

lines.speaker: Advert
lines.text: Lane Change Lozenges. One soothing lozenge, and the urge to switch lanes simply melts away. Blackcurrant, or patience flavour.

lines.speaker: Advert
lines.text: Lane Change Lozenges. Stay where you are. It's lovely, where you are.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Traffic on the eights is brought to you by Grumbel's Ladders.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Can't see the front of the jam? Climb a Grumbel's. Sixty rungs, folds flat into the boot, and from the top you can see the whole bypass.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: It doesn't help. But you can see it. Grumbel's Ladders. Up is a choice.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Good morning. This is the Morning Crawl, on Traffic on the eights. Buzz is up, the kettle's on, and the bypass is exactly where we left it.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Morning commuters, a reminder. You don't have to be anywhere on time. Nobody does. Everybody's employer is on the bypass too.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Your boss is three lanes over. Wave. He's waving back.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: It's the Evening Crawl. Same cars as this morning, facing the other way. Let's get you home. Eventually.

lines.speaker: A Commuter
lines.text: Rita, I've just realised I'm in the morning queue. I've been facing the wrong way since breakfast.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: That's all right, love. It's the same queue. Turn your radio round and pretend.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: This is the Small Hours Jam. The wormholes are quiet, the timelines are dozing, and the bypass is wide awake. It always is.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Rita, it's three in the morning and I can see every headlight in the jam from up here. Billions of them.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: From the pod, it looks like a river. A very slow, very patient river of people trying to get home. It's the prettiest thing I know.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Don't tell them that, Buzz. They'll stop and look.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Breaking traffic news. A moon has gone missing. We had one in lost property on the hard shoulder. It's gone too.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Rita, I think it took the slip road.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Reports from every lane of a strong smell of toast. Buzz, is that you?

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Not me, Rita. The whole jam smells of it. Fourteen billion years of traffic, and it smells like breakfast.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Every driver on the bypass is humming the same song. I can hear it through the desk.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Nobody knows how it ends. That's the bypass for you. Nothing here has ever got to the end.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Rita, somebody just knocked on the pod. Three times.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Buzz, you're four miles up.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: I know, Rita. I'm not opening it.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Drivers, the sky has gone a colour nobody has a word for. Please don't stop to look. You're stopped anyway, I know, but don't.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Buzz says it's the colour of a green light. Nobody here has ever seen one.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: There's a pigeon walking along the bypass. Lane one. Overtaking everyone.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Fastest thing on the bypass in fourteen billion years, Rita. I'm giving it a round of applause.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Halloween traffic. Reports of a ghost car in lane four of the bypass, with nobody driving it, and the indicator going.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Rita, I've had a look. It's been indicating left since before the war. Which war, I can't tell you.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Let it in, everyone. It's waited long enough.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Dispatch is live. Sodium vapour on every arterial, and nobody's shadow is the right length. Go ahead.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Gridley at the desk. I'm taking patches off the orange lanes. Keep the manifest in your hand and the story out of it.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Rita, the pod's over the west arterial. It's all sodium and brake lights.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Copy, Buzz. Dispatch is open. Who's still pretending to move?

lines.speaker: Arterial Driver
lines.text: Dispatch, arterial four, eastbound. Hauler stopped under the vapour. Manifest seven seven four one. Load is glass, and the glass is humming.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Seven seven four one, I have you. Is the humming in the load or in the lane?

lines.speaker: Arterial Driver
lines.text: Both. The lane started it. The glass is just keeping time.

lines.speaker: Toll Operator
lines.text: Toll point, west ramp. The arm is up. It has been up since the lamps came on. Nobody is paying, because the arm forgot how to come down.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: What's the booth reading for vehicles through?

lines.speaker: Toll Operator
lines.text: Manifest of the hour is nine zero two. One of them had no driver. I waved anyway.

lines.speaker: A Phantom Passenger
lines.text: Dispatch. I'm at the merge. I need a lane that doesn't end. You had one last century.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Say your manifest number.

lines.speaker: A Phantom Passenger
lines.text: I don't have one. The car I'm in does. It isn't mine. It never was.

lines.speaker: Arterial Driver
lines.text: Dispatch, that's my cab. There's nobody in the jump seat. There's been nobody all shift.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Both of you, hold the orange light. Do not open a door.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Rita, from up here the west arterial is one solid bar of sodium. Nothing in it is moving except a door, opening.

lines.speaker: Arterial Driver
lines.text: That's not my door. Manifest three eight eight. I'm in the cab with both hands on the wheel.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Three eight eight, stay buckled. Buzz, is the door still opening?

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: It opened. Nobody got out. The vapour went in.

lines.speaker: Toll Operator
lines.text: Dispatch, the arm came down on a bumper that wasn't there a second ago. Manifest four zero zero seven.

lines.speaker: Arterial Driver
lines.text: That's my bumper, and I haven't reached the booth. I'm still under the third lamp.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Four zero zero seven, you are either early or already through. Do not reverse. The lane behind you is full of people who are also you.

lines.speaker: Arterial Driver
lines.text: Gridley, the vapour just went out on arterial nine. Dark for half a mile. I can hear engines and I can't see plates.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Arterial nine, lamps out. Call your manifest.

lines.speaker: Arterial Driver
lines.text: Six one five. And there's a voice in the dark asking me for a lift to the front of the jam.

lines.speaker: A Phantom Passenger
lines.text: Tell her I said please.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Do not give the dark a lift. Lamps or no lamps.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: That's the patch. Stay under the vapour, keep the manifest where you can read it, and do not pick anyone up.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Dispatch clear. The orange lanes keep whatever you told them. I won't.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Pod's staying up, Rita. The vapour looks worse from here.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Then don't look down, Buzz. Dispatch out.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Live patch, west arterial. You're on the desk.

lines.speaker: Arterial Driver
lines.text: Gridley, manifest two two nine. I've got sodium in the mirrors and a passenger I didn't stop for.

lines.speaker: A Phantom Passenger
lines.text: You slowed. That's stopping, where I'm from.

lines.speaker: Arterial Driver
lines.text: I didn't slow. The lane slowed. Tell her to get out of the jump seat.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Nobody gets out under the vapour. Phantom, name a destination or clear the channel.

lines.speaker: A Phantom Passenger
lines.text: The front of the jam. I'll walk the rest, if the rest is still there.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Toll point, you're patched to the desk and to the pod. Go ahead.

lines.speaker: Toll Operator
lines.text: The arm is down on nothing. Manifest one one eight zero. The nothing is revving.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Rita, I can see the booth. Sodium on the roof. No vehicle. The arm is arguing with the air.

lines.speaker: Arterial Driver
lines.text: Dispatch, that's my manifest. I'm still a mile back. The vapour is so thick I can chew it.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: One one eight zero, do not approach your own toll. Buzz, if the air pays, let it through.

lines.speaker: Toll Operator
lines.text: The air doesn't pay. The air knows the rate better than I do.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: I've got two cabs on one channel. Arterial two, and the bypass. You can hear each other. Try not to make it worse.

lines.speaker: Arterial Driver
lines.text: Manifest five five zero. The car in front has been there since the lamps were invented.

lines.speaker: Bypass Driver
lines.text: That's me in front. Your headlights have been in my mirror since I learned to drive.

lines.speaker: A Phantom Passenger
lines.text: There's room if one of you breathes out. I've been between you the whole time.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Five five zero, do not make room. There is no between. Buzz, tell me you see two cabs and nothing else.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: Two cabs, Rita. And a shape the vapour won't quite commit to.

lines.speaker: Toll Operator
lines.text: Dispatch, west shoulder, under the third gantry. A coat is standing there. No car. Manifest blank.

lines.speaker: Captain Buzz Ferraro
lines.text: I have the gantry. The coat is facing the lanes, like it expects a door to open.

lines.speaker: Arterial Driver
lines.text: I'm under that gantry. Manifest eight four two. I am not opening the door. I am not opening the door.

lines.speaker: A Phantom Passenger
lines.text: You don't have to stop. You already did, three exits ago. I kept the seat warm.

lines.speaker: Rita Gridley
lines.text: Eight four two, windows up, eyes on the vapour. The shoulder is not a stop. The coat is not a passenger.
